clue.text: It will go in exactly, the planner announced

indicators.note: announced means the planner's word is said out loud and spelt as something else

parts.note: a planner is someone who devises, a deviser

explanation.surface: Someone's design scheme fits perfectly, as the person who drew it up declared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go in' is the maths sense: a divisor goes into a number with no remainder.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a divisor is a number that divides into another without remainder.

clue.text: Prayer a star keeps on about

indicators.note: about means the combined piece is turned round
keeps means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: the sun is a star
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side

explanation.surface: A celebrity keeps going on about something in a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'star' tempts as the definition of a celebrity, but the definition is 'Prayer'; 'about' reverses the whole SULEGN block, giving NGELUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angelus is a Catholic devotion recited morning, noon and evening.

clue.text: Blessed strength to catch fish

indicators.note: to catch means the first piece takes the second inside it

parts.note: a forte is someone's strong point
tuna is a fish

explanation.surface: A lucky person with the strength to land a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blessed, in the sense of favoured by luck, is a synonym of lucky.

clue.text: Prospect of bombs faced by the army

parts.note: V1s were German flying bombs of the Second World War
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: The prospect of being bombed while facing the army.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospect is a broad view, as is a vista.

clue.text: Animal as guide

definitions.meaning: a young castrated bull, raised for beef
to direct the course of something, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: A bullock is the animal sense; directing a vehicle is the verb sense.

clue.text: Stars were shocked to see vermin

indicators.note: shocked means the letters are jolted into a new order

explanation.surface: Celebrities were horrified to spot rodents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocked' rearranges STARSWERE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rats living in drains are classic pests, a kind of vermin.

clue.text: Predator gallops, making no real show of pity

parts.note: a crocodile is a predatory reptile
tears in the sense of rushes, as a horse gallops

explanation.surface: A hunting beast racing along without any sympathy.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for feigned sorrow, from the myth that crocodiles weep while eating prey.

clue.text: One day in college son works — not good enough

indicators.note: in means the day sits inside the word for college

parts.note: uni is short for university
Sat is short for Saturday, one day of the week
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
a works is a factory

explanation.surface: A student son spending a day at college on his projects, which fall short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' looks like it should give I or A, but 'One day' is a single unit, a day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Something below the required standard is inadequate, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Having fallen, expire in arctic conditions

indicators.note: in places the lapsing inside the conditions

parts.note: arctic conditions are cold
a policy or right that expires lapses

explanation.surface: Someone who has fallen over and died in freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or person that has fallen down has caved in, the same past participle.

clue.text: One getting hammered regularly in Italian villa

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone getting drunk at regular intervals in an Italian country house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' looks like an alternate-letters signal but belongs to the definition; the run sits across 'ItaliAN VILla'.
explanation.definitionFit: A blacksmith's iron block is struck by a hammer over and over.

clue.text: I can't help couple to suppress news

indicators.note: to suppress means the pair holds the news down inside itself

parts.note: a duo is a couple
news read as several 'new's gives N plus N, N being the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A pair hushing up a story says they cannot assist.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial 'don't know' said when asked something one cannot assist with.

clue.text: Almost immediately buries explosive sticking up

indicators.note: buries means the explosive goes inside the shortened word
almost means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: pronto means right away
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Someone hastily burying a bomb that protrudes from the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sticking up' is the definition in the sense of jutting out, not raising a hand or robbing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prominent projects or stands out from its surroundings.

clue.text: Used to swim in river early in the week

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river

indicators.note: to swim means the letters move about freely

explanation.surface: Someone who used to swim in the river at the start of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'early in the week' is a definition by description; 'to swim' scrambles the clue's 'Used' to UESD.
explanation.definitionFit: The second weekday comes near the start of a Monday-to-Sunday week.

clue.text: Some leaves are swallowed — tend to need chewing first

indicators.note: first places the chewed letters ahead of the next piece
to need chewing means the letters are mashed into a new order

parts.note: swallowed means ate

explanation.surface: Leaves are gulped down, but one tends to chew them before swallowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to need chewing' rearranges TEND as DENT, which comes 'first'.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for leaves with toothed edges, describing what some leaves are.

clue.text: So settle feuds with ultimate in patience?

definitions.text: So settle feuds with ultimate in patience?

indicators.note: settle means the letters are put into a new, calmer order
ultimate in means the last letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A suggestion that quarrels end with a final dose of patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' rearranges FEUDS plus E, the last letter of 'patience'; the whole clue describes calming a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To defuse a quarrel is to calm it so it no longer threatens to blow up.

clue.text: Priest raised millions, always in Jan

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a priest
M is the abbreviation for million
e'er is the poetic form of ever, always

explanation.surface: A clergyman collected millions, as he always does in January.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jan' is not January but Jan Vermeer, the Dutch painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jan Vermeer was the Dutch Golden Age painter of Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue.text: Four becoming three perhaps, this being well fielded?

definitions.text: Four becoming three perhaps, this being well fielded?

parts.words: Four becoming three perhaps, this being well fielded?
parts.note: a cricket stroke to the off side that would have reached the boundary for four runs, held to three by a good fielder

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a ball hit to the boundary scores four, but good fielding can stop it short, so only three runs are run. The shot is played square of the wicket on the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket stroke played square on the off side, often fetching boundaries.

clue.text: Sings effusively and soars, seizing chance to look down on earth

indicators.note: seizing means the first piece holds the others inside it

parts.note: soars means rises

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece looking down on another sits above it

parts.note: hap is an old word for chance or luck
sod is turf, earth

explanation.surface: A bird sings and soars, taking the chance to gaze down on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue one piece 'looking down on' another is written above it, so the chance comes before the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: To rhapsodise is to speak or write with great enthusiasm, gushing.

clue.text: A church service

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Just a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is from tennis, not worship.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve the receiver cannot touch is an outright winning shot.

clue.text: Turning on, see one good presenter

indicators.note: turning means the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: re means on or about
v is short for vide, Latin for see
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Switching on the set, watch a fine host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses REVIG.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who presents a gift is a donor, one who gives.

clue.text: Sailor almost pounds on a music centre

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a lascar is an East Indian seaman
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A sailor nearly spends his pounds on a hi-fi system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims LASCAR to LASCA. 'music centre' looks like stereo gear but means a famous opera house.
explanation.definitionFit: La Scala in Milan is a world-famous opera house, a centre of music.

clue.text: Most scattered boxes set out

parts.note: spars means boxes, as boxers do in practice

indicators.note: out means the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Most scattered boxes are set out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET as EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of sparse, so most thinly spread, matches most scattered.

clue.text: Adverb with corresponding adjective is fine

parts.note: well is the adverb
with means and
good is the adjective matching the adverb well

explanation.surface: A grammar note: the adverb and its matching adjective are both acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom expresses acceptance, that things are satisfactory or fine.

clue.text: Bird given measured feed in lab procedure

parts.note: a tit is a small bird
a ration is a measured allowance of food

explanation.surface: A bird is given a carefully measured portion of food during a laboratory experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemistry technique for finding concentration by adding measured amounts of reagent.

clue.text: Amount raised by officer eventually, one of the Whites

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a sum is an amount
a cadet is a trainee who will eventually be an officer

explanation.surface: Money collected by an officer who eventually joins the Whites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Whites' sounds like a team or faction; it is white wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscadet is a dry white wine from the Loire valley.

clue.text: Hamlet's rest, appropriately in this?

parts.note: Hamlet's dying words say the rest is this; and a musical rest is fittingly marked by it too

explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet's final line is 'The rest is silence'; a printed clue asks the solver to fill it in.
explanation.definitionFit: Quiet, the absence of sound, is what Hamlet's dying line says the rest is.

clue.text: Resort area artist captures more festooned in creeper?

indicators.note: captures means the artist holds the other piece inside

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
ivier is a jokey comparative of ivy, more covered in ivy

explanation.surface: A painter captures a holiday area more covered in climbing plants.
explanation.walkthrough: IVIER, 'more ivy', is a made-up comparative, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Italian coast is the classic resort area of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Pronounced northern port happy and cheerful

indicators.note: pronounced means a word said aloud stands for another spelling

parts.note: Blyth is a port in Northumberland, north-east England

explanation.surface: A northern harbour town said to be cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Blyth is a small port town in Northumberland, north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe is a literary word for carefree and joyful.

clue.text: Keen to nurture love for miss

indicators.note: to nurture means the first word holds the second inside

parts.note: avid means keen
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Eager to foster love for a young lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a young woman; it is the verb to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To miss something deliberately is to dodge or steer clear of it.

clue.text: Implore to wipe a nose

indicators.note: to wipe means the letter is rubbed out

parts.note: pray means implore, beg

explanation.surface: Begging someone to wipe a runny nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nose' is the verb, to snoop, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose about is to snoop or meddle inquisitively.
